newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt calls new confidence vote on decree.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt calls new confidence vote on decree.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government has called a confidence vote in the upper house of parliament (Senate) to push a decree covering the transport sector into law, Transport Minister Claudio Burlando said on Tuesday.
Burlando said the vote would be held on Wednesday.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi's cabinet comfortably won a similar motion on the same decree in the lower house of parliament last week in a bid to beat tight new deadlines for the ratification of decree laws.
The coalition relies on support from the hard-left Communist Refoundation party for its majority in the lower house but controls the Senate without outside backing.
The government has resorted to numerous confidence votes during its 10 months in office after the Constitutional court banned the cabinet from the traditional practice of re-issuing old decrees.
Under the new system, a cabinet bill automatically expires after 60 days unless passed into law by parliament.
The transport decree is due to expire on Wednesday and under Italian law, bills have to be ratified by both houses of parliament before moving onto the statute book.

The centre-right opposition wants changes to the transport bill, which will reform the fiscal system for the sector and cut the number of motorway tariffs for haulage companies. It criticised last week's decision to hold a confidence vote.
Burlando said the new confidence vote was inevitable.
"We have been able to have constructive talks with the opposition...but given the time limits, we have called the confidence vote," he told parliament.
